title: Full open substacks and the unramified relative diagonal
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal F$ be a category fibred in groupoids over schemes over $S$, with the total-category, discrete-presheaf and 2-fibre-product conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. A full open substack is specified by a predicate $P$ on its objects, stable under every cartesian pullback, such that for every scheme map $t:h_T\to\mathcal F$ the 2-fibre product $h_T\times_{\mathcal F}\mathcal F_P$ is equivalent over $h_T$ to a scheme $W$ with an open immersion $W\to T$. Its category is the full subcategory $\mathcal F_P$ with the original projection to schemes. Containment of two such full substacks means implication of their object predicates. The two projections from a 2-fibre product are the actual two comma projections over the base; the second lies over the base because the comparison isomorphism lies over an identity.

A map $Z\to T$ from an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space] to a scheme is unramified when all its representable etale scheme charts give unramified scheme morphisms [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. The relative diagonal of $\mathcal F$ is representable and unramified if, for every two scheme maps $T\to\mathcal F$ and $U\to\mathcal F$, the 2-fibre product is represented by an algebraic space $Z$ with an unramified map $Z\to T\times_S U$, and the representing equivalence identifies both projections with those of this specified map. These definitions assert neither existence of a largest open nor existence of an atlas.

proof.text: For the second-projection compatibility obligation, restrict the comma comparison natural transformation to the full subcategory defining the 2-fibre product, then apply H.p. For each object the identity-lift condition gives equal base objects by Mathlib IsHomLift.domain_eq and IsHomLift.codomain_eq. IsHomLift.fac' identifies the component with eqToHom of that equality. Thus every component is invertible.

Apply Mathlib NatIso.isIso_of_isIso_app and Functor.ext_of_iso to this transformation. Rewrite the two based-functor equations f.w and g.w and unfold the explicitly defined first projection. Symmetry gives equality of the second projection followed by G.p with the chosen base functor. This is precisely the proof field required to define moduliTwoFiberSnd. The other declarations are the original explicit full-subcategory, scheme-test and diagonal definitions; no existence statement or definition changes.
